quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Change your lane position as needed for the conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as needed for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible with your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder, not the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's small size makes it easier to hide in another vehicle's blind spot. Drivers may not notice you even when they can see you.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a good way to increase your visibility?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight at all times
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothes with reflective material, keep your headlight on, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass another vehicle on the left, you should ride in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center parts of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you the best view of the road ahead.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass through quickly.
Weave between the cars to pass through quickly.
Not weave between the cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between the cars.
questions.explanation: Riding between parked or slow cars puts you at risk. Car doors can open or cars may pull out suddenly. You will not have space to move safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: To increase your visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothes with reflective material, keep your headlight on always, and adjust your lane position as conditions require.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if possible.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight up. Just before contact, ease off the throttle to lighten the front end.

questions.question: To work well, a face shield should not:

options.text: Have scratches.
Let you see to both sides.
Be sealed so air cannot pass through.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sealed so air cannot pass through.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, prevent objects from entering, allow you to see both sides, fasten firmly, and allow air to flow through. Air flow is important because a sealed shield can fog up and block your view.

questions.question: Usually, a good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things worse by encouraging them to follow faster.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, you should:

options.text: Keep using the front brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your tires lose grip on the road.
You stop before you plan to.
Your tire bursts.
It takes longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause your tires to lose grip and you may crash.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Shift gears while turning.
Shift gears before turning.
Change power suddenly while turning.
Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before turning.
questions.explanation: You should change gears before you enter a turn, not during it.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to daytime?

options.text: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles at night.
Keep a shorter distance behind other vehicles at night.
Always use the same distance day and night.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distance because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts. Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles at night than during the day.

questions.question: What do most motorcycle crashes involve?

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Worn tires.
Riding in the dark.
Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve inexperienced riders.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Position yourself in your lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to be far from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane to make your headlight more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in your lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move into the part of your lane that will let oncoming drivers see you as soon as possible. For example, if turning right, stay in the left part of your lane so they spot you sooner.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet makes you more visible to other drivers day and night.

questions.question: How should a rider position themselves to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit with arms fully extended.
Use arms to hold your body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests and your knees against the gas tank. Your arms should be bent slightly to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another motorcyclist?

options.text: It lets you use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
It makes it easier to talk to each other.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist because it limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake later than you would alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when merging or crossing traffic.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding?

options.text: Your tire pressure.
The tread on your tires.
How reflective your tires are.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the general condition of the sidewalls and tread. You do not need to check how reflective your tires are.

questions.question: When securing a load, where should you place it?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and centered. A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance. Always spread the load evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Only a few minutes.
More than an hour.
It should be complicated.
You don't need to do it before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a quick inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: What should you do to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, squeeze both the front and rear brake levers at the same time.

questions.question: How much braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: Less than 50 percent.
About 70 percent.
It should only be used on wet roads.
It is the only brake you should use.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is an advantage of wearing a brightly-colored helmet?

options.text: It helps other drivers see you.
It can be distracting.
It doesn't improve your visibility.
They are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It protects you in a crash and makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.
